qt: to the Commission Loucas Fourlas (PPE) Subject:
Application of the mutual assistance clause under Article 42(7) TEU in the event of an attack against a Member State

Under Article 42(7) of the Treaty on European Union, if a Member State is the victim of armed aggression on its territory, the other Member States are obliged to provide aid or assistance using every means at their disposal. This provision is especially important in light of the ongoing tensions in the Eastern Mediterranean and the need to ensure the territorial integrity and sovereignty of all Member States of the Union. Given that the Republic of Cyprus and Greece are both Members of the European Union, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
In the event of armed aggression by Türkiye against the territory of the Republic of Cyprus or Greece, would the mutual assistance clause of Article 42(7) TEU be automatically triggered?
What specific obligations does this provision entail in practice for the remaining Member States and what is the role of the EU institutions in its implementation?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.11.2026) The EU stands firmly and unequivocally in support of any Member State in the face of any threat. The security and territorial integrity of all Member States is fundamental for the EU, which actively supports and coordinates efforts to strengthen the EU’s overall defence readiness. The European Council has confirmed its determination to ‘deliver at pace and at scale’ to ensure Europe is equipped to act autonomously, in a coordinated way, and with a 360 degree approach against all threats1. Invoking the mutual assistance clause under Article 42(7) of the Treaty on European Union (TEU) is the prerogative of any Member State that is the victim of an armed aggression. Moreover, the type of assistance required in a given situation is in the first place informed by the assessment made by the attacked Member State. The aid and assistance under this provision could include support at EU level, whether in terms of EU instruments, tools and capabilities, or coordination support, if so requested. In this context, there is a need to develop a common understanding of the implementation and operationalisation of Article 42(7), specifically as regards concrete action to be taken in a situation where that provision is invoked, and the instruments and tools that can be used in such an event, including at EU level, should the victim Member State(s) so request.
